associations.name: Shawnee
associations.period: Early historic/colonial Ohio Valley and Western Virginia connections; 1774 event provides a specific example
associations.author: Robert F. Maslowski
associations.evidenceNote: The specialist overview explicitly identifies Shawnee among peoples historically associated with Western Virginia and discusses hunting, travel and regional influence. The separate Chief Logan article locates Shawnee participation at Point Pleasant in 1774. This is a historical connection, not a claim of exclusive state-wide occupation or present government location.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual historical-regional paragraphs; Chief Logan article's 1774 Point Pleasant paragraph as corroboration.
associations.inspectionNote: Actual encyclopedia text opened and read. Sweeping empty-land, population, ancestry and modern-organization assertions elsewhere in the overview are not adopted.

associations.name: Mingo
associations.period: Eighteenth-century Ohio Valley; explicitly documented connection to West Virginia settlements in the 1770s
associations.author: John Alexander Williams
associations.evidenceNote: The article directly connects people described historically as Mingo with conflicts involving West Virginia settlements. It locates many participants' home villages in Pennsylvania or Ohio and explains the label's mixed, changing use. The link therefore records historical activity involving this region, not a resident Mingo state-wide homeland or a present single government.
associations.reviewedScope: Full short article, especially the paragraph on West Virginia settlements and discussion of the historical name.
associations.inspectionNote: Actual specialist text opened and read. No connection is inferred from Mingo County, Logan place names or a named monument.

associations.name: Susquehannock
associations.period: Displacement after Conestoga Town's destruction; community page supplies no precise settlement dates
associations.evidenceNote: The community account cautiously reports evidence suggesting displaced Susquehannock people inhabited West Virginia. Maslowski's specialist overview also names Susquehannock among historically associated groups. Retain the source's uncertainty: this is a reported displacement connection, not a verified continuous settlement, exclusive homeland boundary or present legal title.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual three-paragraph historical-territory account; e-WV's named historical-group paragraph as supporting context.
associations.inspectionNote: Actual community text opened and read. Embedded/linked maps and underlying deeds were not independently reviewed.

associations.name: Inuit
associations.period: Historical and continuing organizational/community relationship described by ICC
associations.evidenceNote: ICC's own account explicitly identifies Inuit leaders from Kalaallit Nunaat (Greenland) alongside Alaska and Canada at its founding and describes subsequent Inuit participation. This directly supports Greenland for the broad Inuit access point without making a Canadian organization the government of Greenlandic communities.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual Our Story paragraphs on the 1977 founding, 1980 Nuuk assembly, charter ratification and circumpolar representation.
associations.inspectionNote: Actual Inuit-led institutional text opened and read. Current population, policy, sovereignty and legal claims are not copied.

associations.name: Kalaallit

associations.sourceType: Government-owned national tourism board; popular cultural overview
associations.evidenceNote: Section 5 discusses Kalaallit in the context of Greenlandic Inuit. This supports a Greenland connection for the existing access label, not the proposition that every Greenland resident is Kalaallit or that regional Inuit identities are interchangeable.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual section 5 identity/geography text and publisher ownership statement. Population percentages, current conditions and legal/political claims are not adopted.
associations.inspectionNote: Actual primary publisher page opened and read. Its broad naming language is used only for the limited connection described.
associations.recordAction: Replace the existing GL/Kalaallit indexed-only evidence record
